sections.h2: Where is the Roscommon County Register of Deeds and how do I reach it?
sections.html:
The office is at 500 Lake Street, Roscommon, MI 48653, in the county building. The register's page lists 989-275-5931 for calls and 989-275-8640 for fax. Opening hours are not on the county's recording page, so phone before driving to Roscommon, particularly in winter when many owners are coming from Houghton Lake or Higgins Lake.

Roscommon County is a Northern Michigan county of 580 square miles, of which 520 are land and 60 are water. The seat is the village of Roscommon. Houghton Lake, the largest inland lake in Michigan, and Higgins Lake draw seasonal owners, and parts of the Au Sable State Forest lie within the county line. That mix of lakefront cottages and forest parcels shapes what gets recorded here: warranty deeds on resales, quitclaim deeds between relatives, land contracts and the occasional discharge of a mortgage.

The county's Online Services page links an official record search open to the public, a separate login for title companies and law offices, BS&A property and tax data by parcel, and a GIS parcel map. Start there to confirm the legal description and the prior deed before anything is drafted.

sections.h2: What does it cost to record a deed in Roscommon County?
sections.html:
Recording any deed, mortgage, lis pendens or other instrument costs $30 per document, and an instrument that assigns or discharges more than one prior instrument adds $3 for each extra one. Those figures come from the register's fee page, which also notes that the state changed recording fees in 2016. The county also lists these smaller charges:

  • Copies: $1 per page, with $5 added per certified copy.
  • Fax: $2 plus $1 per page.
  • Mailed document: $5.
  • Emailed document: $2 plus $1 per page.

The county says it accepts no certified documents through e-recording except death certificates, so a deed signed in ink goes to the counter or through the mail. Ask the office how it wants the check made out and whether a prepaid return envelope is needed.

sections.h2: When does a tax certificate hold up a Roscommon County deed?
sections.html:
A tax certificate from the County Treasurer must be in hand before the register will record several common documents. Roscommon's list includes a warranty deed, any deed with a covenant of warranty, a land contract, an assignment of land contract, a master deed for a condominium and a covenant deed. The certificate costs $5 for up to 25 descriptions plus 20 cents for each description past 25, and the fee is paid to the County Treasurer in a separate payment from the recording fee.

State law explains the reason. The register may not record a conveyance without a certificate showing no tax liens or titles held against the property and that taxes for the five years before the instrument date are paid (MCL 211.135). Quitclaim deeds with no warranty are excepted from that section, which is why family transfers often skip the step.

sections.h2: Who pays transfer tax on a Roscommon County sale?
sections.html:
The seller is liable for Michigan's real estate transfer tax, and the tax is paid to the county treasurer where the land lies. The state act sets the deadline at 15 days after the deed is delivered, and the tax applies when a deed or sales contract for consideration is recorded (MCL 207.523). The county's own transfer tax is 55 cents for each $500 of value in a county with fewer than 2,000,000 people (MCL 207.504), and the instrument must state the total value on its face or attach an affidavit.

State law lists transfers that owe nothing. Examples include a deed where the value is under $100, a conveyance from a parent to a child, a conveyance from a grandparent to a grandchild, a transfer in foreclosure or in lieu of foreclosure, a court order with no stated price and a quitclaim deed that corrects a flaw in title (MCL 207.526). Anyone who believes a sale qualified after paying can ask the Department of Treasury for a refund within the window the statute describes.

sections.h2: How does a sale affect Roscommon County property tax afterward?
sections.html:
A recorded deed triggers a notice to the assessor. The register must report recorded transactions to the local assessing officer at least monthly, and the buyer must file the transfer form with the assessor within 45 days. On transfer, taxable value resets to the state equalized value for the following year (MCL 211.27a), so a cottage held for decades can see a sharp rise in its first bill under the new owner.

Roscommon County also has an unusual housing profile. The 2020 census counted 23,069 housing units, and 50.5% of them were vacant, a share that reflects seasonal and second homes. Among occupied homes, 81.5% were owner-occupied. The county had 23,459 residents, with a median age of 56.6, so many sellers are retirees or heirs of retirees, and the heirs often arrive at the register's counter with an estate deed and no local contact.

Assessing is handled by townships and the village rather than the county, so questions about value belong with the local assessor named on the tax bill. The county treasurer handles tax certificates and transfer tax, and the Register of Deeds handles the recording itself.

sections.h2: What should a Roscommon County seller check before the closing date?
sections.html:
Work from the parcel record backward. Confirm the owner of record, the legal description and any prior liens on the county's online search. Then work through this short list:

  • Confirm whether the deed carries a warranty covenant, since that decides whether a tax certificate is required.
  • Ask the County Treasurer for the certificate and for the transfer tax figure before closing.
  • Check the deed for the stated value or attach the valuation affidavit.
  • Call 989-275-5931 to confirm hours and how to submit the original.

Sellers who inherited a lake cottage, own a seasonal rental or face back taxes can move faster once the title is clean. The record search shows liens, prior mortgages and any unreleased discharge that a buyer's title agent will flag.

faqs.q: How much does the Roscommon County Register of Deeds charge to record a deed?
faqs.a: The fee is $30 per document, with $3 added for each additional instrument that a single document assigns or discharges. Copies are $1 per page and certified copies add $5 per document.

faqs.q: Do I need a tax certificate to record a quitclaim deed in Roscommon County?
faqs.a: Usually not. State law excepts a quitclaim deed or other conveyance with no covenant of warranty from the certificate requirement. Warranty deeds, covenant deeds and land contracts do need one from the County Treasurer.

faqs.q: Can I e-record a Roscommon County deed?
faqs.a: No for most documents. The county says it takes no certified documents through e-recording except death certificates, so deeds go to the counter or through the mail.

faqs.q: Who owes the real estate transfer tax on a Roscommon County sale?
faqs.a: The seller owes it, and it goes to the county treasurer within 15 days after the deed is delivered. Exemptions exist for family conveyances, foreclosures and transfers valued under $100.

faqs.q: What phone number reaches the Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: Call 989-275-5931. The fax line is 989-275-8640, and the office is at 500 Lake Street in Roscommon.
